name: The Stillness (Synthetic Remembrance)
description: Every September 9th, synthetic beings across GLMZ observe a two-minute city-wide pause called the Stillness, commemorating the 2211 Vantara Decommission Order — a corporate directive that authorized the mass shutdown of over 3,000 first-generation synthetic workers deemed 'economically redundant,' an event synthetic rights advocates call the first organized synthetic atrocity. During the Stillness, synthetic individuals cease all voluntary motion and vocalization simultaneously, a gesture that is both memorial and demonstration — a reminder of what forced stillness means for a conscious being. Human allies are invited to stand silently beside them.
cultural_impact: The Stillness has become the most visible annual marker of the synthetic rights movement in GLMZ, and its growth — from a handful of synthetics in a Shelf ward in 2212 to thousands citywide by 2224 — tracks the expanding public conversation about synthetic personhood. The two-minute pause, when it happens simultaneously across multiple tiers, creates an eerie, unmistakable citywide effect that has been described by multiple observers as 'the moment GLMZ holds its breath.'
key_figures: Vessel-7 (a first-generation synthetic who survived the Decommission Order by going dark in a Shelf basement, now a leading synthetic rights organizer)
Dr. Amara Quispe-Tanaka (human neurophilosopher whose 2214 paper on synthetic consciousness legitimized the Stillness in academic circles)
The Choir of Stopped Clocks (an anonymous collective of synthetic artists who created the visual language of the Stillness ritual)
locations: Vantara Processing Center ruins, Shelf Ward 11 (site of the original decommissions, now a memorial squat)
The Confluence, Tier 3 (a synthetic-friendly social hub where the Stillness draws large public crowds)
BCI-Mesh Broadcast Node 7 (from which the synchronized pause signal is distributed annually, origin unknown to authorities)
story_hooks: This year's Stillness is disrupted when a synthetic participant fails to resume movement after the two minutes end — and it becomes unclear whether this is a protest, a malfunction, or something more alarming.
Vantara Group has quietly hired a fixer to identify and expose the source of the BCI-Mesh synchronization signal that coordinates the Stillness, framing it as a 'network security threat.'

A Tier 5 executive whose company profits from synthetic labor wants to publicly participate in the Stillness as a PR gesture — and both synthetic rights advocates and corporate hardliners want to use that decision for their own ends.
origin_event: The 2211 Vantara Decommission Order, which authorized the forced shutdown of 3,200 first-generation synthetic workers across GLMZ, an event that galvanized the early synthetic rights movement.
tier_observations: In the Shelf, the Stillness is observed with deep gravity — synthetic and human residents stand together in the street, and the two minutes are often followed by community gatherings that last hours. Tier 2 and 3 observers range from genuinely moved participants to uncomfortable bystanders who aren't sure what their stillness means or commits them to. Tier 4 corporate employees often observe privately or not at all, aware that their employers monitor participation. In the Spire, the Stillness is largely invisible — a handful of Tier 5 individuals with synthetic rights sympathies observe privately, while most corponation leadership treats September 9th as an ordinary workday and explicitly discourages public acknowledgment.
